provenance.method: Technology communication/input question using current platform accessibility documentation and preserving privacy/context limits.

question: Typing or device control is difficult. What speech-to-text or voice-control options can I inspect?
why_it_matters: Alternative input can reduce motor, spelling or task-load barriers, but speech recognition itself can introduce privacy, accuracy and environment constraints.
current_understanding: Inspect built-in dictation, voice typing or voice-control features on the device first, then test accuracy in the real environment and language used. Check whether processing is local or cloud-based where privacy matters, and keep a non-voice alternative for noisy spaces or times when speech is unavailable.
evidence_needed: Current privacy and offline-processing comparisons across major platforms.
Accuracy and accessibility evidence for users with speech differences or variable speech access.
reopening_conditions: Platform voice features materially change their processing or privacy model.
dissent: Voice input can be liberating for one person and inaccessible, socially exposing or exhausting for another.
